title: Run 27 execution package v2 specification approval v2
$comment: Package-scoped successor to plans/27_langgraph_curriculum_factory_remediation/schemas/spec_approval.schema.v1.json. v1 is the *parent* Run 27 package's own frozen schema and const-locks approved_spec to that package's spec (plans/26_langgraph_curriculum_factory/spec/langgraph_curriculum_factory.spec.v2.md) -- a path this package's approved specification (spec v4, at plans/26_langgraph_curriculum_factory/spec/v3/langgraph_curriculum_factory.spec.v4.md) can never equal, so v1 can never validate this package's approval record no matter how it is filled in. This schema lives under this package's own schemas/ directory, is declared in this package's own implementation.graph.v5.yaml rules.frozen_before_entry (not v1's, which remains exclusively the parent v1 package's own frozen contract), and const-locks paths to this package's own artifacts instead. v1 itself is untouched by this schema's existence.

approved_spec.$comment: Const-locked to this package's own single governing specification, exactly as v1 const-locks approved_spec to the parent package's own spec -- the fix here is pointing the same discipline at the correct file, not relaxing it.

spec_qa_verification_sha256.$comment: SHA-256 of plans/26_langgraph_curriculum_factory/spec/v3/QA/verification.json, the specification's own independent QA verification record.

approved_rc_manifest.$comment: Deliberately NOT a const, unlike approved_spec/approved_graph: the RC manifest is a versioned review-lineage pointer, not this package's governing identity. A const locked to one generation (e.g. rc3) would force a schema version bump for every future re-approval that lands on a later RC (rc5, rc6, ...) even when nothing else about this schema's shape changed. The pattern fixes the family/location and numbering convention; the validator (not this schema, which cannot read file bytes) recomputes approved_rc_manifest_sha256 against the file this path names and rejects a mismatch.

execution_package_qa_verification_sha256.$comment: SHA-256 of the approved RC's own QA/verification.json (the RC manifest's sibling QA record), not the specification's QA record.

approved_graph.$comment: Const-locked, like approved_spec: the active execution graph is this package's other governing identity document, not a review-lineage pointer, so it gets the same strict treatment. A future graph v6+ requiring fresh approval gets its own schema version (exactly as this schema itself exists because v1's const pointed at the wrong package's spec) -- that is the correct discipline for a document N00 gates entry against, not the defect being fixed here. The RC manifest's own generation is allowed to float (see approved_rc_manifest) because it is supporting QA-lineage evidence for the graph, not the graph itself.

model_assignments.$comment: USER_DECISION_REQUIRED-01 (spec v4 S7.1), structured per exact job ID (spec v4 S6.3) instead of embedded only in approval_statement prose. Every job's model/effort is const-locked to the exact already-resolved decision -- this is a positive assertion of one specific frozen decision, not an open enum, mirroring how v1/v2 const-lock approved_spec/approved_graph rather than merely type-checking them.
